subject: GPU pool timelock escalation & customer bridge plan
messages:
From: Alex Ward <alex.ward@fabled-retail.com>
To: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@fabled-retail.com, procurement@fabled-retail.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jan 2029 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Immediate: production latency and 500s on Dedicated GPU pool (Fabled Retail)

Markus — we just started seeing a sharp increase in tail latency across our inference endpoints and a surge of 500s starting ~08:50 PT. Traffic is steady; there were no deployments from our side. Can you confirm whether this is a platform incident and what mitigations you have in place? Our checkout flows are impacted.

Appreciate a quick check.

— Alex
Alex Ward
SRE, Fabled Retail
From: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Alex Ward <alex.ward@fabled-retail.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jan 2029 09:14:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Immediate: production latency and 500s on Dedicated GPU pool (Fabled Retail)

Alex — thanks for the ping and sorry for the impact. We see an anomaly in the us-west-2 dedicated GPU pool serving your account: periodic kill/restart cycles on a subset of reserved nodes that are correlated to an autoscaler heartbeat mismatch (internal ticket OPS-4982).

Short summary of immediate steps we are taking (live now):
- Routing a portion of Fabled traffic to warm standby nodes in a different availability zone to reduce tail latency (transparent failover).
- Temporarily increasing headroom for your reserved pool by 30% to absorb bursts while we investigate.
- Engaging the infra-oncall to collect node-level coredumps and K8s event logs.

We will provide an incident timeline and an ETA for full restoration within 60 minutes. I’m on the call with infra now — I’ll loop you in.

Markus Klein
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Immediate: production latency and 500s on Dedicated GPU pool (Fabled Retail)

Markus / team — quick technical note from infra: we’re observing a "timelock" condition in the allocator where node heartbeats intermittently time out under a particular sequence of preempt/evict signals. When the allocator marks nodes as unavailable it triggers a restart loop which floods the scheduler. Affected nodes show identical kubelet logs and a pattern of evict->restart within ~2m windows.

Actions executed so far:
- Bypassed the autoscaler for the affected tranche and pinned nodes to avoid churn.
- Drained and reprovisioned two suspect nodes to break the restart loop.
- Applied a temporary patch to the eviction detector to increase the heartbeat grace period and prevent premature eviction.

Impact: partial reduction in 500s after traffic shift, but we’re still seeing elevated latency on large-batch workloads. Will follow up with a longer RCA when we have coredumps and scheduler traces.

Ben Carter
Principal SRE
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 18 Jan 2029 16:43:00 -08:00
Subject: Post-incident summary: timelock root cause, remediation, and customer bridge plan

Alex / Fabled team — thank you again for your patience while we completed the investigation. This note summarizes our findings, mitigations, credits, and next steps.

Incident summary (what happened):
- Between 08:48–10:20 PT on 2029-01-15 we observed repeated node eviction/restart cycles in your reserved GPU tranche due to an allocator "timelock" triggered by concurrent preempt signals and an aggressive heartbeat grace policy. The churn caused brief 500s and increased tail latency for large-batch endpoints.

Root cause (technical):
- The allocator's eviction detector used a fixed heartbeat grace window that failed to tolerate rapid preemptions caused by cloud-level rebalancing. Under a specific sequence of signals the detector marked nodes unavailable before underlying kubelets completed reconnection, creating a restart-loop.

Remediations implemented:
- Immediate: routed 25% of Fabled traffic to warm standby nodes in a different AZ and increased reserved headroom by 30% to stabilize throughput.
- Hotfix: increased heartbeat grace window and introduced a debounce in the eviction detector to prevent premature marking of nodes as down. Hotfix deployed to us-west-2 at 09:28 PT and validated by smoke tests.
- Recovery: drained and reprovisioned 4 nodes; captured full kubelet logs and two coredumps for offline analysis.

Customer impact and data integrity:
- Observed effect: transient 500s and elevated latency on large-batch calls between 08:50–09:10 PT. We validated request routing and model outputs post-recovery and found no evidence of token-loss or ordering abnormalities impacting model responses. We will continue to monitor inference correctness for 7 days and will share automated evals to your team.

Compensation and next steps:
- As a goodwill gesture and in recognition of customer impact, Redwood will issue a one-time service credit equal to 20% of January 2029 Dedicated capacity charges for Fabled Retail (applied to your next invoice). Procurement is copied to coordinate.
- Actions we will take over the next two weeks:
  - Permanent allocator fix with extended grace policy + additional telemetry (ETA: 2029-01-25).
  - Backfill tests across AZs to ensure warm standby path meets large-batch SLAs under load.
  - Weekly status updates to Fabled SREs until the fix is in prod.

Attachments included: incident-timeline-20290115.pdf (high-level timeline), k8s-node-logs-20290115.tar.gz (node logs collected), initial-customer-bridge-plan.docx (operational checklist).

If you’d like a 30-minute review with our infra and product teams to walk the findings and test plan, we can host tomorrow (Fri 2029-01-19) at 09:00 PT. Please let me know a preferred time.

Thanks again,

Markus Klein
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
